name: Cross the Sea Under Camouflage
source: When precautions are complete, vigilance slackens; the familiar is trusted. The hidden lies within the obvious, not apart from it.
explanation: Show the ordinary to hide the extraordinary, so the enemy drops its guard through sheer familiarity.
story: Xue Rengui built a "mansion" for the sea-fearing Emperor Taizong and feasted him while a great ship carried them across — a surprise landing hidden in plain sight.
reflection: The enduring truth: what is shown openly is rarely questioned. Mastery is making the decisive move look like routine.

name: Besiege Wei to Rescue Zhao
source: To attack a massed enemy, divide it; strike where it is weak rather than meet its strength head-on.
explanation: Instead of relieving Zhao directly, strike Wei’s capital so the enemy must turn back — then ambush it worn and divided.
story: At Guiling, Sun Bin besieged Wei’s capital, broke the siege of Zhao, and captured Pang Juan on the march.
reflection: Pressure the point your opponent cannot abandon; they will retreat from where you are weak to defend where they are weak.

name: Kill with a Borrowed Knife
source: The foe is clear but allies unsteady — induce an ally to strike, spending no force of your own.
explanation: Use another’s hand to remove your rival, keeping yourself clear of the blow and the blame.
story: Zigong shuttled between Qi, Wu and Jin, turning four states against one another to save Lu without lifting a sword.
reflection: Agents endure; the hand that strikes is seldom the hand that gains. Design the board, let others move the pieces.

name: Wait at Leisure for the Exhausted
source: Exhaust the enemy’s momentum without battle; wear the hard away to strengthen the soft.
explanation: Conserve your strength and strike only when the enemy is spent — meet motion with stillness.
story: At Changshao, Cao Gui let the Qi army exhaust three war-drums of spirit, then struck and broke them at once.
reflection: Rest is not idleness; it is the compounding of strength while the opponent spends theirs to nothing.

name: Loot a Burning House
source: When the enemy’s calamity is great, seize the advantage — the firm resolves what the soft cannot.
explanation: When a rival is stricken and disordered, take the gain while the opening lasts.
story: Wu invaded the Chu capital Ying amid the turmoil following King Ping’s death, reaping the reward of chaos.
reflection: Crisis reveals vacancy; the prepared move into the empty space others cannot hold.

name: Feint East, Strike West
source: The enemy’s will is scattered and unprepared; profit from its loss of command and take it.
explanation: Create a false thrust to fix the enemy’s eye, then deliver the real blow elsewhere.
story: Li Su marched in a snowy night, feinting one route while seizing Caizhou and capturing Wu Yuanji.
reflection: Attention is a finite resource; whoever directs it, commands the field.

name: Create Something from Nothing
source: Deceive, then not deceive — make the deception real. From small falsehood to great truth.
explanation: First feign emptiness until it is believed, then plant a real move within the belief.
story: Zhang Yi promised Chu "six hundred li" to break its alliance with Qi; the land never came, yet Chu was already isolated.
reflection: From nothing a beginning is made; the danger is when the nothing was promised as something.

name: Secretly March to Chencang
source: Show one movement to fix a static, over-confident foe; then advance where unguarded.
explanation: Repair the roads openly, march by a hidden route; the obvious distracts from the real.
story: Han Xin openly rebuilt the plank roads while secretly marching through Chencang, reclaiming the Three Qin.
reflection: The visible plan protects the invisible one; concentration follows the decoy.

name: Watch the Fires Across the River
source: When rivals turn on each other in disorder, wait in the shadows; their fury exhausts itself.
explanation: Do not rush in; watch opponents tear each other apart, then gather what remains.
story: Cao Cao let the Yuan brothers war on each other, then defeated them one by one and took Hebei.
reflection: Intervention too early buys another’s war; patience lets others pay its price.

name: Hide a Knife in a Smile
source: Lull with trust, plot in secret; prepare, then move before the change comes.
explanation: Wear warmth and goodwill while the blade is readied within; strike as the guard drops.
story: Li Linfu spoke honey yet bore a sword; he befriended then ruined those in his way.
reflection: A smile is a mask; wisdom asks what the mask protects.

name: Substitute the Plum for the Peach
source: Loss is inevitable — sacrifice the lesser to preserve the greater.
explanation: Trade a minor loss for a vital gain; protect the trunk by letting a branch fall.
story: In the Zhao orphan tale, Cheng Ying gave his own son to save Zhao Wu and the clan’s line.
reflection: Not every piece can be saved; the art is knowing which to let go.

name: Walk Off with the Sheep
source: Exploit every tiny gap; take every small gain that presents itself.
explanation: While moving, pocket the opening at hand — small gains compound into position.
story: Having failed at Zheng, the Qin army on return conveniently destroyed the state of Hua.
reflection: The main road rarely yields all; the side path often holds the extra.

name: Beat the Grass to Frighten the Snake
source: Probe to surface the hidden; observe, then act. Repetition is the mother of the unseen.
explanation: A small probe draws the hidden into the open; act on what the probe reveals.
story: Judge Wang Lu, hearing a complaint against his clerk, blurted "you beat the grass, but I am the startled snake" — the probe exposed the probe.
reflection: Information is bought cheapest by those willing to seem to act.

name: Borrow a Corpse to Revive the Soul
source: What is useful cannot be borrowed; borrow what others have discarded.
explanation: Take a form others abandoned, breathe new purpose into it, and it lives again.
story: Liu Bei "borrowed" Jingzhou and the prestige of imperial kinship to root his rise.
reflection: What is dead to one owner may yet serve another who sees the form.

name: Lure the Tiger Off the Mountain
source: Use circumstance to hem him in, use men to draw him out.
explanation: Coax the strong opponent from his ground, then strike where he is powerless.
story: Sun Ce lured Liu Xun away to attack Shangliao, then seized his Lujiang stronghold.
reflection: Strength is place; remove the place and the strength leaks away.

name: To Catch, First Release
source: Pressing breeds resistance; releasing lessens force. Follow close but do not press, wearing down will and strength.
explanation: Let the prey run so its guard drops and strength fades, then close the net at leisure.
story: Zhuge Liang captured and released Meng Huo seven times until he submitted wholly, pacifying the south.
reflection: Command that is felt as freedom is the command that lasts.

name: Throw a Brick to Attract Jade
source: Offer something of its kind to lure it; strike the unenlightened with a model.
explanation: Lead with a modest offering to draw out a richer one in return.
story: Chang Jian wrote an incomplete verse on a temple wall to draw Zhao Gu into finishing a finer one.
reflection: The giver of the first stone often receives the finer.

name: Capture the Ringleader First
source: Shatter the solid, seize the chief, and the body dissolves.
explanation: Strike the head — remove the center and the whole scatters.
story: Defending Suiyang, Zhang Xun shot the rebel general Yin Ziq i blind, collapsing the assault.
reflection: Cut the head and the body stills; find the head in every system.

name: Remove the Firewood from the Cauldron
source: Do not meet its force; remove the momentum beneath it.
explanation: Rather than fight the flame, pull away what feeds it.
story: Zhou Yafu crushed the Seven Kingdoms revolt by cutting Wu-Chu supply lines, not by frontal battle.
reflection: Every fire has wood; remove it and the blaze becomes memory.

name: Fish in Troubled Waters
source: Profit from its inner disorder, its weakness and lack of command.
explanation: When the water is muddied and none commands, reach in and take.
story: Liu Bei seized Jingzhou amid its repeated upheavals, gaining a footing.
reflection: Order crowns its king; disorder crowns the quick.

name: Slough Off the Cicada’s Shell
source: Keep the form, complete the posture; friends doubt not, foes move not.
explanation: Leave a shell that holds the shape, and slip the living thing away unseen.
story: Di Qing left an empty camp as a decoy and secretly marched around to crush Nong Zhigao.
reflection: The shape remains; the life has already gone. The wise flee without appearing to move.

name: Shut the Door to Catch the Thief
source: Hem in a small foe. To let it roam is to lose the advantage.
explanation: Encircle a weaker foe and seal the exit, then take it at leisure.
story: At Changping, Bai Qi encircled Zhao Kuo’s army, cut its supplies and exits, and destroyed it.
reflection: A thief in the open is a war; a thief in the locked room is a catch.

name: Befriend the Distant, Attack the Near
source: When geography and power bind you, gain from the near, harm the far only at cost.
explanation: Court the distant as friend, strike the near as prey; expand by adjacency.
story: Fan Ju urged King Zhaoxiang to befriend far states and attack near ones, uniting China by degrees.
reflection: Alliances are for those you will not yet fight; conquest is for those beside you.

name: Borrow a Passage to Attack Guo
source: Between two great powers, the enemy coerces; I lend my strength as pretext.
explanation: Borrow a road through one state to strike another, then absorb the lender on the way home.
story: Duke Xian of Jin borrowed passage through Yu to destroy Guo, then extinguished Yu on his return.
reflection: He who lends the road often becomes the next destination.

name: Replace the Beams with Rotten Pillars
source: Shift his formation often, draw off his best, and await his collapse.
explanation: Quietly swap the load-bearing parts so the whole rots from within.
story: At Shaqiu, Zhao Gao forged the edict, removed Fusu and installed Huhai, swapping the pillars of Qin.
reflection: The facade stands; the beam is gone. Collapse comes not with a crash but a silence.

name: Point at the Mulberry, Curse the Locust
source: To command the great over the small, warn one to guide the other.
explanation: Reprove one openly to caution another without naming him.
story: Sun Wu beheaded King Wu’s favored concubines to drill the army, and all obeyed.
reflection: The spoken name is seldom the one that listens.

name: Feign Madness but Keep Balance
source: Better to feign ignorance and do nothing than fake knowledge and act rashly.
explanation: Play the fool to hide your edge; stay harmless in appearance, sharp within.
story: Sima Yi feigned illness for years, then seized power once Cao Shuang let his guard fall.
reflection: Madness professed is a shield; the still mind behind it is the sword.

name: Remove the Ladder After the Ascent
source: Offer a convenience, urge him forward, then cut his support.
explanation: Lure him up, then pull away the ladder so retreat is impossible.
story: Liu Qi climbed the tower to ask Zhuge Liang’s counsel; Zhuge had the ladder drawn up, prompting him to seek a post away.
reflection: He who climbs willingly need not be pushed; only the ladder need vanish.

name: Put Fake Blossoms on the Tree
source: Borrow a setting to build presence; small force, grand appearance.
explanation: When weak, inflate presence with arrangement and signal; appearance alone may decide.
story: At Changban, Zhang Fei stood alone by the bridge with spears planted like a forest, and Cao’s army withdrew in dread.
reflection: Men follow the appearance of strength; often the appearance is enough.

name: Turn from Guest into Host
source: Slip in through the gap, then seize the master’s switch.
explanation: Enter as guest, grasp the key post, and become the host.
story: Liu Bang entered the capital first, proclaimed light laws, and turned guest into master of the realm.
reflection: The guest who learns the house becomes its keeper.

name: The Beauty Trap
source: Against a strong army, strike its general; against a wise general, strike his heart.
explanation: Send beauty close to the key figure to cloud his judgment and lower his guard.
story: Goujian sent Xi Shi to King Fuchai, muddling his rule until Yue destroyed Wu.
reflection: Desire is the oldest gate; through it even the strongest falls.

name: The Empty Fort Strategy
source: Show emptiness as emptiness, and doubt breeds doubt.
explanation: Project calm emptiness so the foe suspects an ambush and dares not advance.
story: Zhuge Liang played the zither in an open city; Sima Yi, fearing a trap, withdrew.
reflection: What is empty, shown without fear, becomes a question the enemy answers by leaving.

name: Sow Discord Between Enemies
source: Doubt within doubt. Set the foe against himself from within; thus we lose nothing.
explanation: Plant false intelligence so the enemy suspects and destroys his own.
story: Zhou Yu used the envoy Jiang Gan to deliver a forged letter, prompting Cao Cao to execute his own admirals.
reflection: The best spy makes the enemy his own executioner.

name: The Self-Inflicted Wound
source: No man harms himself; therefore a man harmed is suspected of a plot.
explanation: Hurt yourself to earn the enemy’s trust, then strike from within.
story: Huang Gai offered to defect; Zhou Yu had him flogged to prove it, then fired the Red Cliffs.
reflection: Belief is bought by pain; the wound that is shown is the wound that is trusted.

name: Chain Stratagems Together
source: Against many and mighty, do not meet them; make them burden themselves.
explanation: Link stratagems in a chain so the enemy is entangled and exhausts himself.
story: Wang Yun used Diao Chan to chain Dong Zhuo and Lü Bu against each other, then destroyed them.
reflection: One stratagem is parried; a chain of them the mind cannot unwind.

name: Retreat is the Best Option
source: Withdraw the whole army from the foe. To step back in order is no fault, for it preserves the norm.
explanation: When the odds are lost, retire intact — keep the mountain green for another day.
story: Duke Wen of Jin "retreated three days’ march" to avoid Chu’s edge, then won at Chengpu and became hegemon.
reflection: To retreat in order is not defeat; it is the field kept for the next victory.

title: Winning Stratagems
theme: The Art of Offense from Strength
body: These are used when you hold the initiative. The theme is turning strength into a decisive blow through disguise and timing, not brute force.

title: Enemy-Deception Stratagems
theme: The Art of Deceiving a Peer Foe
body: Used when foes are evenly matched. Deception, false warmth and feigned weakness open a seam in a balanced field.

title: Attack Stratagems
theme: The Art of Seizing the Initiative
body: Once attacking, strike the center and cut the source. Release to exhaust, then capture the chief.

title: Chaos Stratagems
theme: The Art of Thriving in Chaos
body: When all is disorder, fish in troubled water, shed the shell, shut the door. Chaos is the opportunist’s weather.

title: Contention Stratagems
theme: The Art of Contending as Equals
body: As equals locked together, shift the beams, warn by indirection, and turn guest into host — power moves through the small.

title: Defeat Stratagems
theme: The Art of Turning Defeat Around
body: When losing, beauty, empty fort, discord, self-wound, chains and retreat turn doom into a second chance.
